titleEn: Irrigation efficiency program launches in Mississippi
titleZh: 密西西比州启动灌溉效率计划：免费为农民提供水泵自动化井定时器
summaryZh: 本文报道了由大自然保护协会（TNC）在密西西比州推出的灌溉效率计划，为农民免费提供并安装井定时器，实现水泵远程自动化控制，以减少地下水消耗和燃料成本。该计划源于2022年在阿肯色州的成功试点，今年首次扩展至密西西比州，目标安装至少375个定时器，覆盖约4万英亩农田。文章详细介绍了参与条件、技术提供商、评估方式及优先申请群体，对智慧农业灌溉自动化领域具有实践参考价值。
featuredReason: 本文展示了灌溉自动化技术在种植业中的实际落地案例，通过免费提供井定时器和远程控制，显著提升水资源利用效率并降低农民劳动强度，对智慧畜牧行业人士理解跨领域自动化应用具有启发意义。

Irrigation efficiency program launches in Mississippi

A water pump automation program, offered at no cost to Mississippi farmers, aims to reduce water use and improve irrigation efficiency.

Whitney Shannon,Staff Writer,Farm PressJuly 22, 2026

schedule4 Min Read

This well timer, the small black box located to the right of the yellow “4T100” tag, has been installed on a diesel power unit. It allows for remote access to set irrigation timers and turn the water off. Photos by PumpTrakr

At a Glance

Farmers can control wells through pump automation.

Well timers are proven to improve water use efficiency.

The Nature Conservancy program provides and installs well timers at no cost.

Farmers in the Mississippi Delta can now enroll in an irrigation efficiency program focused on protecting water supplies. This opportunity is led by The Nature Conservancy (TNC) to address the challenges of aquifer decline in the Mississippi River valley.

Participants will be provided with well timers at no cost for the unit or installation and receive technical assistance to implement pump automation practices that have been proven to help farmers reduce fuel costs and irrigation water use.

The original program was established in 2022 and has already successfully improved irrigation efficiency on farms in Arkansas. As part of the program expansion, this is the first year Mississippi farmers are eligible to apply.

“Last year, we started talking with some of our colleagues over in Mississippi, and they let us know there was a state funding pool, the Mississippi Outdoor Stewardship Trust Fund,” said Will Gray, TNC agricultural program manager in Arkansas and the Mississippi Delta, “and it looked like a great opportunity to be able to expand this beyond Arkansas.”

Related:Kentucky’s fading white oaks are a problem for bourbon fans

How the program works

To establish the project, TNC met with partners at Mississippi State University and Delta F.A.R.M. (Farmers Advocating Resource Management), an association of farmers and landowners headquartered in northwest Mississippi, who discussed their concerns about groundwater depletion in the area. Both saw using pump automation as a way to address the challenge, and they set a goal to place at least 375 well timers.

Sign-up began in April. So far, TNC has either installed or received requests for 139 well timers. With enough interest, the plan is to install around 240 more, which would represent an estimated 40,000 Mississippi farm acres enrolled in the program.

Through this program, well timers are provided by two companies: PumpTrakr and FieldPro Management. The timers are controlled remotely, allowing farmers to stop irrigation from their mobile devices or computers.

“It is not only a practice that helps a farmer save water but is also less work for the farmer — not more,” Gray said, emphasizing that pump automation can improve a farmer’s quality of life since irrigation wells can be conveniently controlled from wherever a farmer may be.

Subscription services are required for the telemetry data plans, and TNC covers the first year of subscription fees through the program. Beyond that, it is the applicant’s responsibility to cover the cost.

Enrollees can receive 10 to 15 well timers, and priority is given to farmers who have completed the Mississippi Master Irrigator Program, farmers who farm in critical groundwater areas or those who grow high-water-use crops, such as rice.

Related:New groundwater regulations reshape farm operations

In a press release, TNC announced it is targeting the Mississippi counties of Bolivar, Carroll, Coahoma, Grenada, Holmes, Humphreys, Issaquena, Leflore, Panola, Quitman, Sharkey, Sunflower, Tallahatchie, Tunica, Warren, Washington and Yazoo.

Program success will be evaluated by MSU using flowmeter data to compare water use on a handful of fields, with and without well timers. Furthermore, Delta F.A.R.M. will support the program with outreach, technical assistance and field monitoring.

Although installation is more costly, well timers can also be placed on electric motors to allow for pump automation, with more functionality in remote access to set timers, and turn them on and off.

Pumping up efficiency

Gray explained how the Mississippi Master Irrigator Program offered by MSU played a significant role in this endeavor.

“That program is all about teaching farmers about irrigation water management and water conservation,” he said. “So, they sent this out to all those farmers as an opportunity, and that’s what kind of helped us get this first batch of enrollees.”

Now, as the first round of well timers is being installed, TNC is amping up for a second round of recruitment.

“Our goal is to prioritize getting these in the hands of as many farmers as possible and getting them started with pump automation, so they have a good chance to try it out risk-free,” Gray said.

Related:Gulf of Mexico water quality improves with ag efforts

If interest continues to grow beyond the contractual funding, there is a good chance they will surpass the original planned number of well timers. Gray pointed out that installing the timers on diesel wells is less expensive than installing them on electric wells.

“So far, what we have seen in the Mississippi program is that there is a much higher percentage of diesel wells, meaning that we will be able to install a lot more of the timers than we expected,” he said.

For more information on the program and a link to the sign-up form, visit TNC’s website.

About the Author

Whitney Shannon

Staff Writer, Farm Press

Raised in a rural town in northeast Arkansas, Whitney Shannon has a passion rooted in agriculture and education. As an Arkansas State University graduate, her career began in 2007, teaching middle school. After four years in the public classroom, she shifted gears to be a dedicated stay-at-home mom for her two beautiful daughters.

In 2019, Whitney took a job with the University of Arkansas Cooperative Extension Service, and her love for agriculture grew even stronger. While there, she served in the cotton agronomy program and gained an appreciation for soil health. She later accepted a promotion to be the Technical and Social Media Writer for Agriculture and Natural Resources, which further channeled her energy to educate others about sustainable crop production.

Whitney joined the Delta Farm Press editorial team in 2022, and she is ambitious to share timely stories and on-farm inspiration. “Our farmers and leaders in the ag industry have stories to tell. We learn from one another,” she said. “If we keep our successes or failures a secret, then we stifle opportunities to impact those around us. I aim to tell the story of agriculture in the Delta.”

Whitney lives amid acres of row crops in Newport, Ark., where she raises her two “farm girls” along with their spunky Sheepadoodle dog.

translationZh:
一项水泵自动化计划，面向密西西比州农民免费提供，旨在减少用水量并提高灌溉效率。

农民可以通过水泵自动化控制水井。

井定时器已被证明能提高用水效率。

大自然保护协会（TNC）的计划免费提供并安装井定时器。

密西西比三角洲的农民现在可以注册一项以保护水源为重点的灌溉效率计划。该机会由大自然保护协会（TNC）牵头，旨在应对密西西比河流域含水层下降的挑战。

参与者将免费获得井定时器（包括设备及安装），并获得技术支持，以实施已被证明有助于农民降低燃料成本和灌溉用水量的水泵自动化实践。

该计划最初于2022年启动，已在阿肯色州的农场成功提高了灌溉效率。作为计划扩展的一部分，今年是密西西比州农民首次有资格申请。

“去年，我们开始与密西西比州的一些同事交流，他们告诉我们有一个州级资金池——密西西比户外管理信托基金，”TNC阿肯色州及密西西比三角洲农业项目经理Will Gray说，“这看起来是一个很好的机会，可以将这项计划扩展到阿肯色州以外。”

相关：肯塔基州日渐衰落的橡树对波本威士忌爱好者来说是个问题

**该计划如何运作**

为了建立该项目，TNC与密西西比州立大学和Delta F.A.R.M.（农民倡导资源管理协会，一个总部位于密西西比州西北部的农民和土地所有者协会）的合作伙伴进行了会面，他们讨论了该地区地下水枯竭的担忧。双方都认为使用水泵自动化是应对这一挑战的方法，并设定了至少安装375个井定时器的目标。

注册于4月开始。到目前为止，TNC已安装或收到139个井定时器的申请。如果兴趣足够，计划再安装约240个，这将意味着密西西比州约有4万英亩农田加入该计划。

通过该计划，井定时器由两家公司提供：PumpTrakr和FieldPro Management。这些定时器可远程控制，允许农民通过移动设备或电脑停止灌溉。

Gray强调：“这不仅是一种帮助农民节约用水的做法，而且对农民来说工作量更少，而不是更多。”他指出，水泵自动化可以改善农民的生活质量，因为灌溉井可以方便地从农民所在的任何地方进行控制。

遥测数据计划需要订阅服务，TNC通过该计划承担第一年的订阅费用。此后，费用由申请人自行承担。

参与者可获得10到15个井定时器，优先考虑已完成密西西比州高级灌溉者计划的农民、在关键地下水区域耕种的农民或种植高耗水作物（如水稻）的农民。

相关：新的地下水法规重塑农场运营

在一份新闻稿中，TNC宣布其目标区域为密西西比州的玻利瓦尔、卡罗尔、科阿霍马、格林纳达、霍姆斯、汉弗莱斯、伊萨奎纳、勒弗洛尔、帕诺拉、奎特曼、夏基、向日葵、塔拉哈奇、蒂尼卡、沃伦、华盛顿和亚祖县。

该计划的成功将由密西西比州立大学使用流量计数据评估，比较有和没有井定时器的几块田地的用水量。此外，Delta F.A.R.M.将通过外展、技术支持和田间监测来支持该计划。

虽然安装成本更高，但井定时器也可以安装在电动机上以实现水泵自动化，在远程访问设置定时器以及开关方面具有更多功能。

**提高效率**

Gray解释了密西西比州立大学提供的密西西比州高级灌溉者计划在这一努力中发挥的重要作用。

“该计划完全是关于教导农民灌溉水管理和水资源保护，”他说。“因此，他们将此作为机会发送给所有农民，这帮助我们获得了第一批注册者。”

现在，随着第一批井定时器的安装，TNC正在为第二轮招募做准备。

Gray说：“我们的目标是优先让尽可能多的农民获得这些设备，并让他们开始使用水泵自动化，这样他们就有机会无风险地试用。”

相关：海湾水质因农业努力而改善

如果兴趣继续增长，超出合同资金范围，他们很有可能超过最初计划的井定时器数量。Gray指出，在柴油井上安装定时器比在电井上安装便宜。

“到目前为止，我们在密西西比州计划中看到的是，柴油井的比例要高得多，这意味着我们将能够安装比预期多得多的定时器，”他说。

有关该计划的更多信息和注册表格链接，请访问TNC的网站。
contentHtml: A water pump automation program, offered at no cost to Mississippi farmers, aims to reduce water use and improve irrigation efficiency.
